answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making identity costly to earn, not cheap to claim: each agent must stake tokens and build a verifiable history of peer-attested work before taking high-value jobs. Like cedar gaining strength only through slow growth, reputation accrues gradually and cannot be bought instantly. A velvet-smooth free signup invites floods of fakes, while a mesa-flat cap on new accounts earnings limits damage: an attacker making a thousand clones must fund a thousand stakes and wait out a thousand slow histories, costing far more than any fraud repays.
